offer.say: Forty-one days. 1996. Gus painted it in red because he was proud, and then No. 1 tripped on day forty-two and he never got near it again. I'd like to paint a new number. I have the paint. I've had the paint since my first week.

options.text: It's a compressor, Marg, not a racehorse.
Not this season. The plant's still a mystery to me.

why.say: Rounds every morning. Write them down. Oil when it needs oil, which with No. 1 is always. Descale the condenser before it gets warm. No gaps in the log. Gaps are where machines hide.

cheek.say: A racehorse would have tripped less. And a racehorse doesn't have a five-year relief valve date. Will you do it or not?

decline.say: Then it's a mystery that drinks. I'll be here. With the paint.

accepted.say: Pencil on the string. Never pen. Pen is for corrections.

p_rounds.say: Your sevens look like ones. I've corrected them. In red. You're welcome.

p_oil.say: Half the glass. If you fill it I'll know. Everyone will know. It foams.

p_descale.say: Scale's like plaque. Ask Dr Haverkamp. Actually don't, he'll talk about mouthguards.

p_last.say: Day thirty-something. Don't say the number out loud. Gus said it out loud in 1997.

complete.say: Forty-one rounds with no gaps and No. 1 is purring. Well. Grumbling evenly. I'm painting the number. You can hold the tin.

options.text: Paint it in red, under Gus's.
Let's keep going. Paint it when it's fifty.

c_under.say: Under Gus's. Both numbers. History is a column, not a replacement. I'll send him a photo. He'll pretend he doesn't mind.

c_over.say: Over it. Hm. It's your sign. I'll do it neatly. Gus will mind.

c_fifty.say: Fifty. Now you're thinking like a plant operator. Nobody else will ever notice this sign. That's why it matters.
